children: L&T Semiconductor Technologies Limited (LTSCT) and Tata Electronics have entered into a strategic partnership to jointly develop and manufacture semiconductor products in India, as the companies seek to build domestic capabilities spanning chip design, fabrication and advanced packaging.

Under the partnership, the companies will explore fabrication and packaging opportunities for LTSCT's existing and future chip products using Tata Electronics' range of semiconductor manufacturing processes and packaging technologies, according to a joint statement on Friday.
The collaboration will also cover design-to-fabrication optimisation, with the companies seeking to improve chip designs for efficient manufacturing at scale.
The partnership targets semiconductor applications across automotive, industrial, communications, security and intelligent-edge markets, with an emphasis on serving both Indian and global customers.

"Semiconductor leadership will increasingly be defined not just by design breakthroughs but by the ability to industrialise those designs through advanced packaging and manufacturing," LTSCT Chief Executive Sandeep Kumar said.

LTSCT, the semiconductor arm of engineering conglomerate Larsen & Toubro, operates as a fabless semiconductor company, while Tata Electronics is building capabilities in semiconductor fabrication, packaging and testing in India.

Tata Electronics CEO and Managing Director Randhir Thakur said the partnership would combine LTSCT's semiconductor design and engineering capabilities with Tata Electronics' manufacturing, packaging and testing infrastructure.
The companies said the alliance supports India's push to develop a domestic semiconductor ecosystem and increase value addition in the country under the government's semiconductor programme.
